CTFs & lab notes

Reverse Engineering and Hardware CTFs

Planned solutions and notes from reverse engineering, exploitation, and hardware CTF challenges, with explanations of the methods used and lessons learned.

To be continued…

Planned scope

This planned collection will document reverse engineering, exploitation, hardware, and IoT CTF challenges. Each future writeup will explain the challenge context, investigation, relevant tools, and the steps needed to reproduce the result.

Draft outline

This is a structured draft. Each section will be completed with measured results, commands, and evidence as the work is carried out.

Challenge context

  • Record the event, category, and rules.
  • Note the provided files and hardware.
  • State the objective and time budget.

Initial triage

  • Identify file types, architectures, and interfaces.
  • Extract strings, headers, and obvious constants.
  • Form a first hypothesis about the solution path.

Static and dynamic analysis

  • Disassemble or decompile the relevant code.
  • Trace execution with a debugger or emulator.
  • Record dead ends as well as progress.

Hardware access

  • Identify debug headers, flash, and peripheral buses.
  • Capture traffic during the challenge flow.
  • Use non-destructive access where possible.

Solution and lessons

  • Document the shortest reproducible solution path.
  • Explain the key insight and the tools used.
  • Record what would change in a real assessment.

Topics to cover

  • Reverse engineering CTFs
  • Exploitation challenges
  • Hardware and IoT challenges
  • Reproducible lab notes
